name: libquantum
desc: C library for the simulation of quantum mechanics
why: Simulates quantum registers and algorithms like Shor's on a classical machine, a real door into quantum computation.

brief.what_it_is: libquantum is a C library for simulating quantum mechanics, with its main focus on quantum computing. It provides a quantum register with basic gates such as Hadamard and Controlled-NOT, and measurements on single qubits or the whole register. It can also compute the time evolution of arbitrary Hamiltonians, including time-dependent ones, by numerical integration of the Schrödinger equation or by exact diagonalization. The homepage says it includes implementations of Shor's factoring algorithm and Grover's search algorithm. It is a library, not a command-line tool: brew reports no executables.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says it started as a pure quantum computer simulator and that support for general quantum simulation was added later. Its stated aim is to let people run quantum algorithms and quantum mechanics simulations on ordinary classical hardware with high performance and low memory use.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage describes an implementation of a quantum register with an easy-to-use interface for gates and measurements. Time evolution uses fourth-order Runge-Kutta integration or exact diagonalization, with optimizations for sparse Hamiltonians. Decoherence support, a quantum error correction interface, and the density operator formalism are also listed as features.
brief.install_notes: The homepage says libquantum requires a C compiler with complex number support. It has been reported to work on GNU/Linux (the main development platform), FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD, Mac OS X, HP Tru64 UNIX, and AIX. I did not read the downloads or documentation pages, so build steps and any configuration are not covered here.
brief.standout: It is a long-running C library that covers both gate-model quantum computing and general open-system or Hamiltonian simulation in one codebase. Its homepage lists Shor's and Grover's algorithms as built in, and it was an official SPEC CPU2006 benchmark.
brief.status: quiet. The newest item on the homepage is the 2013-01-29 release of libquantum 1.1.1, before that a 2010 Rydberg simulator note and a 2008 release of 1.1.0 and 1.0.0. I did not check a repository or the downloads page for later commits, so there may be newer activity I could not see.
brief.caveats: Licensed under GPL version 3, so it is Free Software with copyleft terms. There are no command-line tools; you use it from C code. The homepage news is several years old. The homepage does not describe the build process or give a usage example. Brew's caveats field is empty.
